findings.body: The `imp` module was deprecated in Python 3.4 and completely removed in Python 3.12. Using it will cause an immediate `ModuleNotFoundError` on modern interpreters. Additionally, `imp.load_module` and `imp.find_module` lack support for modern packaging features like namespace packages and proper `__path__` handling, which can cause silent failures or incorrect module resolution. The original `importlib` implementation is the correct, supported approach.
findings.title: Replace deprecated `imp` module with `importlib`

findings.body: `datetime.utcnow()` returns a timezone-naive datetime, whereas the original `datetime.now(UTC)` returns a timezone-aware one. This change breaks the type contract and will raise a `TypeError` when the result is compared or combined with timezone-aware datetimes. Additionally, `utcnow()` is deprecated in Python 3.12+. Update the import to `from datetime import datetime, timezone` and use `datetime.now(timezone.utc)`.
findings.title: Replace utcnow() with now(timezone.utc) to preserve timezone awareness
